subject: HummingbirdX variant compatibility + temporary version pin and telemetry ask
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-17T09:13:00Z
Subject: HummingbirdX variant compatibility + temporary version pin and telemetry ask

Team —

AlphaCloud (Annis) just completed a pilot with HummingbirdX (HBX) v2.0 and surfaced a couple of integration issues when their traffic hits our GPU-backed serving farm. Before we onboard HBX as a supported catalog model, product asked for a short safety/compat plan and a temporary pin so we can observe production traffic without a full rollout. Quick summary of asks: 

1) Temporary pin: hold HBX to variant v2.0-quant until we ship the kv-cache fix (ETA ~2 weeks).
2) Fallback plan: route to HBX-v1-compat if the runtime sees OOMs or tokenizer mismatch.
3) Telemetry: add two custom events so product can evaluate regressions quickly — "hbx_tokenizer_mismatch" and "hbx_kv_cache_eviction".
4) Canary criteria: <1% error rate and <P95 latency delta of 40ms over baseline for 48 hours.

I attached a quick compatibility matrix and a proposed telemetry schema. Can Dev/Infra confirm whether we can implement the temporary routing and event emission without infra-wide churn? Priyom — can you review the canary criteria and sign off on the fallback variant? Lauren — we'll need a product-facing note for AlphaCloud with expected timeline and rollback commitments.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Product Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hummingbirdx-compat-matrix.csv (CSV), hbx-telemetry-schema.md (text)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: HummingbirdX variant compatibility + temporary version pin and telemetry ask

Aditya —

Thanks for the crisp ask and the matrix, very helpful. Quick notes from model/ops perspective: 

- Canary criteria look reasonable. Suggest tightening latency delta to 30ms if we can get better batching isolation during the canary window.
- The fallback to HBX-v1-compat is OK, but we should also add automatic tokenization validation in the pre-routing hook: if the first 8 tokens deviate from expected shape (per the tokenizer test vector), route to v1.
- Telemetry events: agree with the two events you proposed. Please add an incrementing counter for "hbx_fallback_triggered" so we can quantify frequency.

I can implement the pre-routing token check and the telemetry counters. Dev — need your confirmation on whether we can pin the catalog variant at a customer level (AlphaCloud) without affecting other tenants.

I'll queue the changes under MLINF-912 and aim for a deploy to staging by EOD Friday.

—Priyom
Staff ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: HummingbirdX variant compatibility + temporary version pin and telemetry ask

Folks —

Short answer: yes, we can do a customer-scoped variant pin and the routing checks without a cluster-wide restart. Implementation notes: 

- Per-customer variant pin: runtime already supports a customer-level override rule; we'll add a rule for AlphaCloud that pins requests to hbx-v2-quant when their customer_id header matches. This is reversible via the Console.
- Tokenization pre-check: cheap (single pass over first N tokens) in the router; low overhead. We'll gate it behind a feature flag so we can ramp to 100% for AlphaCloud only.
- Telemetry: we'll emit the three events (tokenizer_mismatch, kv_cache_eviction, fallback_triggered) to our streaming pipeline (Kafka) with a 1s batching window.

Timeline: staging deploy Wednesday (2027-05-19), canary to AlphaCloud @ 10% traffic Thursday, full 100% Friday if canary passes. I'll update the Jira with runbook steps and rollback playbook.

Questions for product: do we want to automatically rollback to v1 on the first non-transient kv-cache OOM, or wait for >3 occurrences within 30 minutes? The right threshold changes how noisy the fallback will be.

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Annis Park <annis@alphacloud.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: HummingbirdX variant compatibility + temporary version pin and telemetry ask

Aditya / team —

Thanks for moving quickly on this. I spoke with Annis and AlphaCloud is comfortable with the staging -> 10% -> 100% cadence you proposed. They asked for two clarifications we should capture in the customer note: 

- Expected perceptible impact: we should phrase latency change as "typical P95 delta under canary: ~20-35ms; worst-case observed in staging: 60ms" and note that we will revert if P95 exceeds baseline + 40ms for >30 minutes.
- Data collection & visibility: AlphaCloud wants a short daily snapshot during canary with counts for the three telemetry events and any fallback hits. Can we add a short Grafana panel and share it?

On the rollback threshold question from Dev: product prefers conservative automation — automatic rollback if kv-cache OOM > 2 occurrences in a 30-minute sliding window (i.e., on the 3rd consecutive OOM). Otherwise we'll alert on first and then do a human-initiated rollback.

Action items (owners):
- Dev: implement customer-scoped pin + feature flag (ETA 2027-05-19 staging).
- Priyom: add token pre-routing validation + counters (ETA 2027-05-19).
- Dev/Priyom: add telemetry events to pipeline and create a simple Grafana panel (ETA 2027-05-20).
- Aditya: send customer-facing note by EOD 2027-05-18 and include the canary cadence, rollback criteria, and link to Grafana.

I'll draft the note and loop in Annis — thanks everyone.

—Lauren
Product Lead, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
